author: Copilot
body: `parse_licensed_capacity` now selects the "latest" entry by taking `storage_entries[-1]`, which silently assumes the NOC `licensed` list arrives in chronological order. Since the NOC DTO/client layer doesn’t enforce or sort that ordering, this can return an outdated capacity if entries are ever unsorted. Consider selecting by `max(entry.date)` (previous behavior) or explicitly sorting/filtering by date before picking the latest.

author: Copilot
body: The `RequestedStates` decorator writes contacted-service keys into `sessionStorage` but never clears them. Because `ServiceSection` now reads contacted IDs from `sessionStorage` on mount, visiting this story can leak state into other stories (e.g., `Grid`) within the same Storybook session. Consider clearing the relevant keys before/after the story (or using a per-story cleanup in a decorator).

body: `ContactRequestDto` renames the request field from `service` to `service_name`, which makes the `/account/contact` contract non-backward-compatible (e.g., a rolling deploy where the frontend/backend are briefly out of sync will cause 422 validation errors). Consider accepting both keys during a transition by adding a validation alias for the old `service` field while still normalizing to `service_name` internally.

body:
`parse_licensed_capacity` selects the most recent entry by taking `storage_entries[-1]`. Since that is only correct when NOC returns `licensed_entries` in chronological order, the docstring should explicitly state that ordering assumption (similar to the note added for `preprocess_chart_data` / `_build_monthly_points`) to prevent future regressions if the upstream contract changes.
```suggestion
        Filters to ``max_now_storage`` metric entries and takes the last entry as the most recent one.
        Assumes NOC returns ``licensed_entries`` in chronological order; if that upstream ordering
        contract changes, ``storage_entries[-1]`` will no longer represent the latest entry.
```

author: Copilot
body: The decorator performs `sessionStorage.setItem(...)` as a render-time side effect. In React (and especially with StrictMode/double-invoked renders), this can run multiple times and is best moved into `useEffect` along with the corresponding cleanup so the story’s storage setup is only applied on mount/unmount.
